column1: # What Felix asks reality about Elenchus.
# Felix may declare which question to ask. Felix may never author the answer.
# Each row names a predicate and the command that enumerates its members; the
# members come back from the command, and nothing in the engine can add one.
# predicate
# A row with no witness can never report `empty` and always blocks as
# `unknown`. Every row here carries one, and each asks a different question
# from its probe: the running app versus the file on disk, git's index versus
# the filesystem. A witness that re-runs the probe agrees with it by
# construction and buys nothing.
# `http_route` is why this whole surface exists. Asked on 2026-09-03, FastAPI
# reports SIXTEEN routes where the decorators in the source show twelve; the
# four extra are the auto-mounted documentation endpoints and they appear in no
# source line. A grep for `@app.` would have answered twelve with total
# confidence, and every question about what this service exposes would have
# been answered against a number that was wrong by a third.
# `entrypoint` and `ceiling_site` are the pair, and the reason they are two
# rows rather than one check. There are two processes that can serve this
# product, and for a while only one of them armed the per-process call ceiling
# — so the surface a stranger with a link can loop was unbounded while every
# grep for the variable name succeeded. A check answers yes or no about a thing
# somebody remembered to check. Two enumerations put the numbers side by side
# and let the difference be the finding.
http_route
